newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian soybean prices firm as farmers hold stocks.
newsitem.headline: Indian soybean prices firm as farmers hold stocks.

text.p: Indian soybean prices firmed during the week on limited arrivals as farmers held back stocks in the hope of getting better prices, traders said on Tuesday.
They said soybean was quoted at 10,550-11,000 rupees per tonne compared to 10,400-10,700 last week. Soybean was quoted at around 8,600-8,800 rupees per tonne at the same time last year.
In plant delivery condition, soybean was quoted at 10,850-11,100 rupees per tonne.
"Arrivals were just 40 percent compared to last year's arrivals as the crop is poor this year and farmers are waiting for better prices," said Dinesh Jadhav, a leading oilmeal broker.
Traders said daily soybean arrivals were around 8,000 tonnes compared to 20,000 tonnes at the same time last year in the markets of central India, the hub of soybean processing industry.
"Soybean prices may cross the 11,500 rupee mark (per tonne) in mid-January," said Prakash Vohra, a leading oilmeal trader.
Traders said Indian soymeal exporters had traded nearly 1.4 million tonnes of soymeal in 1996/97. Export demand was at a low ebb during the last 20 days, they said.
India soymeal was quoted at around $270 per tonne FOB compared to $218 last year, traders said.
The Soybean Processors' Association of India (SOPA) has estimated a soybean crop of around 4.1 million tonnes in 1996/97 (Nov-Oct) compared to 4.5 million tonnes last year.
Traders expect the 1996/97 soybean output to be lower at 3.7 million tonnes.
